osmTags.inscription: Close to this spot lies the site of the mediaeval gallows In 1610 Blessed George Napier, Catholic Priest and Martyr, was executed here.

OLIVE GIBBS (née Cox) 1918–1995 Lord Mayor of Oxford Chairman of Oxfordshire / County Council Defender of Oxford's urban landscape Tireless champion of social causes Honorary Freeman National Chair of CND was born and lived here 1918–1942

Prison A Wing (1852-56)
Modelled on Pentonville prison, a central space was surrounded by 150 identical cells each housing a single prisoner, held in isolation. When it closed in 1996 up to 3 men shared a cell. In 2006 it opened as a Hotel.

This tower was built to imprison debtors who owed money. A rare triangular stone staircase leads to four floors divided into cells, some with fireplaces. Prisoners remained in prison until they paid their debts, and long stays were common.

elements.name: The Perimeter Wall at Oxford Prison

osmTags.inscription: The wall is built close to a stream using large stones with a rubble inner core and smaller loose stones above, and, later razor wire. All this made escape underneath or over the wall very difficult.

elements.name: Archaeology, the Castle Ditch, and its skeletons

osmTags.inscription: In 2003 excavations uncovered the Castle Ditch part of the defences of the Norman Castle. 64 human skeletons were found buried here, many dating from the late 16th century.

Vaulted Well Chamber (13th century)
The Chamber houses a 54 feet deep brick-faced well which drops to the water level below the Mound. This provided a supply of fresh water to the occupants of the Tower which once stood on the summit of the Mound.
Felicia Skene 1821‒1899, prison reformer and friend of the poor, lived here 1869‒1899
ABEL BEESLEY 1851-1921 Waterman Invincible Punting Champion of England who popularised the punt as a leisure craft Lived here 1899-1921

eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
